from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Can a square fit inside any loop?", "This is the famous Inscribed Square Problem.", "We call these loops Jordan Curves."]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Intuitive Hook", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects for animations
        dot1 = Dot(color=BLUE)
        dot2 = Dot(color=GREEN)
        line = Line(start=dot1.get_center(), end=dot2.get_center(), color=YELLOW)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        line.add_updater(lambda m: m.become(Line(dot1.get_center(), dot2.get_center(), color=YELLOW)))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Visualize a square template sliding along.",
            "Rotate and shrink the square carefully.",
            "All four corners eventually touch.",
            "The intersection points click perfectly.",
            "A square is now fully inscribed."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Inscription", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        curve = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([2*np.cos(t) + 0.5*np.sin(3*t), 1.5*np.sin(t), 0]),
            t_range=[0, 2*PI]
        ).set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(curve, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        square = Square(side_length=1.5).set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), FadeIn(curve), FadeIn(square))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), 
                  Rotate(square, angle=PI/6),
                  square.animate.scale(0.7))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"),
                  square.animate.move_to(self.grid['C3']).scale(0.8))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFD700"),
                  square.animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#32CD32"),
                  Flash(square, color="#32CD32"))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion & Generalizations", ["Rectangles are always inscribable.", "Squares are harder to fit.", "Still open for non-smooth curves."])
        
        # Define objects
        rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=BLUE)
        square = Square(side_length=1.5, color=GREEN)
        curve_label = Text("Non-smooth curves", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(rect, "C2")
        self.play(Create(rect), Write(self.lecture[0]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(square, "C5")
        self.play(Create(square), Write(self.lecture[1]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(curve_label, "E3")
        self.play(Write(self.lecture[2]), FadeIn(curve_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # Cleanup
        self.play(FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(rect), FadeOut(square), FadeOut(curve_label), FadeOut(self.title))
        self.wait(1)

sections.title: Introduction: The Intuitive Hook
sections.content: Present the visual problem: Can you always fit a square inside a closed loop (like a squiggle on a piece of paper)? Introduce the concept of a 'Jordan Curve'.
sections.example: An artist drawing a continuous, non-intersecting line (a snake) on a canvas; can we always place four corners of a square on that line?

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Configuration Space
sections.content: Explain that we aren't just looking at the loop, but at a 2D space of 'candidate squares' defined by their center and size, mapping these points to the loop boundary.
sections.example: Visualizing a 3D coordinate system where the x and y axes represent the center of the square, and the z-axis represents its side length.

sections.title: The Mathematical Mechanism: Symmetry & Topology
sections.content: Introduce the Borsuk-Ulam Theorem: A continuous map from a sphere to a plane must map antipodal points to the same value. Use this to prove that a square must exist.
sections.example: Using a globe projection: If you have two points on exactly opposite sides of the earth, their 'temperature' or 'pressure' values will match.

sections.title: Visualizing the Inscription
sections.content: Demonstrate the transition from a candidate set to the final intersection. Show how shrinking/rotating the square until all four vertices touch the curve satisfies the topology condition.
sections.example: Animation of a robot arm 'sliding' a square template along a curvy path until all four corners click into place simultaneously.

sections.title: Conclusion & Generalizations
sections.content: Briefly touch upon the 'Inscribed Rectangle' problem (which is proven for any Jordan curve) and mention that the 'Square' version is still an active research area for non-smooth curves.
sections.example: Comparison: A rectangle is easy to 'stretch' into place, whereas a square is 'rigid,' explaining why the math gets harder.
